items.quote: After talking until daylight, he left.
items.contrast: Talking until daylight versus the earlier act of eating bread.
items.reason: Eating is a plausible earlier action, but the passage directly places Paul’s departure after his talking until daylight, making that the immediately preceding activity.

items.quote: He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah
items.contrast: The man receiving the warning versus the old prophet who delivers it.
items.reason: The old prophet could be confused with the person threatened because the word first comes to him. However, he addresses the man of God from Judah, so the second-person phrase “your body” refers to that man.

items.quote: said to them and to all his mother’s clan, “Ask all the citizens of Shechem
items.contrast: The relatives instructed to relay the message versus the citizens who are its intended audience.
items.reason: The citizens of Shechem are plausible because they receive the message, but Abimelek gives the instruction to his mother’s brothers and the rest of his mother’s clan, telling them to ask the citizens.

items.quote: From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
items.contrast: The hill country reached immediately before Micah’s house versus the earlier camp near Kiriath Jearim.
items.reason: Near Kiriath Jearim is a plausible earlier stop, but “From there” marks the next movement to the hill country of Ephraim and then to Micah’s house. The key is unique, but “the residence the Danites visit” is an avoidable generic substitute for the explicit name “Micah’s house.”

items.quote: God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur Baal and against the Meunites.
items.contrast: The peoples Uzziah was helped against versus the Ammonites, who brought him tribute.
items.reason: The Ammonites are a plausible mistaken inclusion because they are named immediately afterward, but the passage explicitly limits God’s help against opponents to the Philistines, the Arabs in Gur Baal, and the Meunites. The Ammonites have the distinct role of bringing tribute.
